If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}-x-1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[{e}^{x}-x-1]^{′}}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}-1}{-\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}-x-1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1} & =-{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{[{e}^{x}-1]^{′}}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]^{′}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{x}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{0}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
